_why_this_command: Both self-tests, not just the one that looks most relevant. ADR 0026's set
ran a narrower command on its first attempt and produced a confident NOT
CAUGHT, because the test closing the mutation lived in the second of the
two files the record named. This record covers two scripts, so it runs
_why_exit_code: The first attempt used the default `test_count` verdict and the harness
refused to run at all: `The baseline suite did not execute any tests.`
That refusal is ADR 0069 working. These self-tests are not pytest and
emit no `N passed` line, so the harness could not establish that anything
had been judged -- and rather than read 'no count' as 'nothing failed',
it stopped. The `exit_code` mode added for ADR 0045 is the right verdict
for a guard script, and it is more careful than reading `$?`: a mutation
that makes a script CRASH also exits non-zero, and calling that 'caught'
would certify a check that no longer runs.

mutations._claim: The `reproduced_by` escape hatch is checked, not trusted.
_note: `and` -> `or`. The mutant accepts any `reproduced_by` whose ARGUMENTS
appear on some line of verify_build.py even if the script does not,
which is the escape hatch reopened. If this is not caught, the field
is a way out of the guard rather than a second way of satisfying it.

mutations._claim: A set file with neither mutations nor reproduced_by still fails.
mutations.find: elif not spec.get("test") or not spec.get("mutations"):
_note: Deletes the unrunnable-set check entirely. This is the branch the new
`reproduced_by` clause sits in front of, and adding an `if` in front
of an existing check is exactly how a check quietly stops running --
so the mutation asks whether anything would notice.

mutations._claim: A set file is judged runnable by its CONTENTS, not its outer shape.
_note: Neuters the per-entry key check while leaving it visibly present --
the shape of a check that cannot fail. This set file itself was the
historical failure: its entries were keyed `search` instead of
`find`, the guard called it reproducible, and mutate.py died on
`KeyError: 'find'` after the baseline had already run.

mutations._claim: A quoted title cannot become a filename with spaces in it.
_note: Reverts slugify to what the tool shipped with: strip and lowercase,
no hyphenation. This is the exact historical failure -- it produced
`docs/adr/0098-evidence the guard could not recognise.md` on this
repository, before the file was deleted and the tool fixed.
